title: Analyzing Why |y| = x and y^2 = x^2 Are Not Functions of x
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Vertical Line Test
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Describe the graphs of the equations (a) |y| = x and (b) y^2 = x^2, and explain why neither equation defines y as a function of x.
finalAnswer: \text{(a) Two rays } y = \pm x \text{ for } x \ge 0; \quad \text{(b) Two lines } y = \pm x; \quad \text{Both fail the Vertical Line Test}

steps.title: Solve Equation (a) for y and Describe Its Graph
steps.explanation: For x < 0, |y| = x has no real solutions. For x = 0, y = 0. For each x > 0, there are two distinct solutions: y = x and y = -x. The graph consists of two rays meeting at the origin and opening to the right in Quadrants I and IV.
steps.why: By definition of absolute value, |y| = x (with x > 0) is satisfied by both y = x and y = -x.

steps.title: Explain Why Equation (a) Is Not a Function of x
steps.explanation: Every vertical line x = c with c > 0 intersects the graph of |y| = x twice, at (c, c) and (c, -c), violating the Vertical Line Test.
steps.why: A function cannot assign two distinct outputs to the same input x > 0.

steps.title: Solve Equation (b) for y and Explain Why It Fails
steps.mathExpression: y^2 = x^2 \iff |y| = |x| \iff y = x \text{ or } y = -x
steps.explanation: Taking square roots of both sides of y^2 = x^2 yields y = +/-x, whose graph is the pair of diagonal lines y = x and y = -x intersecting at the origin. For every x != 0, there are two distinct y-values (y = x and y = -x), so it fails the Vertical Line Test.
steps.why: Every vertical line x = c with c != 0 crosses both lines y = x and y = -x at distinct points.
